source: Jin et al. (2024) AgentReview: Exploring Peer Review Dynamics with LLM Agents (EMNLP 2024)
finding: First LLM-agent simulation of a whole peer-review process (reviewers, authors, area chairs). Reviewer biases changed the final decision on 37.1% of papers.
numbers: Over 53,800 generated review documents, over 10,000 reviews, over 500 ICLR submissions from four years. Analysis model: gpt-4-1106-preview. Headline: 37.1% variation in paper decisions due to reviewer biases.
quote: 37.1% variation in paper decisions due to reviewers' biases
limits: Simulated reviewers, not real ones. The biases are partly planted by persona prompts, so the model follows instructions rather than showing a natural bias. Ground truth is ICLR accept/reject only.
agent_relevance: Shows how Merton's universalism fails inside a pure-LLM committee: persona and social cues shift verdicts. Supports G4/G5: do not let judges see identity or each other's scores.

source: Jin et al. (2024) AgentReview, section 3.3 author anonymity (authority bias)
finding: Telling reviewers that authors are renowned (violating universalism) changed accept decisions, much more for lower-quality papers than for higher-quality ones.
numbers: Known identity for 10% of papers changed decisions by 27.7%. Jaccard index of accepted sets vs baseline when 1, 2, 3 reviewers knew the identity: 0.364, 0.154, 0.008. Higher-quality papers changed far less.
quote: reviewers tend to perceive manuscripts from renowned authors as more accurate
limits: Reviewers were TOLD in the prompt that authors were renowned; this tests obedience to a stated cue. The 27.7% figure is from the intro; the experiment is section 3.3.
agent_relevance: Direct analogue of the blind-judge guardrail (G5): strip authorship and provenance before any model judges an answer.

source: Jin et al. (2024) AgentReview, social influence and altruism fatigue results
finding: After discussion, LLM reviewers moved toward the group (conformity), and one lazy reviewer lowered effort in the others. Biased reviewers amplified each other's negative opinions and pulled unbiased reviewers down.
numbers: Std deviation of ratings fell 27.2% after rebuttal. One under-committed reviewer cut commitment of all reviewers by 18.7%. Biased reviewers dropped 0.17 in rating; unbiased reviewers dropped 0.25 through spillover. Authoritarian area chair: Cohen's kappa 0.266 and 69.8% agreement vs baseline.
limits: Simulation with prompted personas (irresponsible, malicious). Rebuttal effect was small, suggesting anchoring on first impressions.
agent_relevance: Conformity and anchoring are the failure G4 warns about: if voters see each other, variance collapses without accuracy gain. Keep voters independent until code compares them.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
finding: Blind expert review found LLM-generated ideas more novel than human experts' ideas, slightly weaker on feasibility.
numbers: 79 expert reviewers, 49 ideas per condition. Novelty: human 4.84, AI 5.64, AI + human rerank 5.81 (p<0.05, robust to multiple-hypothesis correction). Overall score correlates with novelty r=0.725 and excitement r=0.854, but feasibility only r=0.097.
quote: LLM-generated ideas are judged as more novel (p < 0.05) than human expert ideas
limits: Humans wrote ideas on the spot (37 of 49 improvised; ideas were about the top 43% of their own past ideas). Novelty judged on proposals, not executed projects. Style normalised by an LLM rewrite.
agent_relevance: Organised scepticism applied to the machine: blind expert panels reward novelty and ignore feasibility. Score feasibility with a separate code check.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) sections 7.1 and 7.2: diversity and LLM judges
finding: LLM idea generators lack diversity (massive duplication), and LLM judges are unreliable evaluators of ideas: all were below human-human agreement.
numbers: Of 4,000 generated seed ideas only about 200 (5%) were non-duplicates at similarity 0.8. Human reviewer agreement 56.1% (balanced accuracy); NeurIPS'21 66.0%; ICLR'24 71.9%. LLM judges: GPT-4o direct 50.0, GPT-4o pairwise 45.0, Claude-3.5 direct 51.7, Claude-3.5 pairwise 53.3, AI Scientist reviewer 43.3.
limits: Idea ranking is noisy even for humans. Best pairwise ranker is near the ceiling for these prompts.
agent_relevance: Supports G4 (samples from one model are not independent: 5% distinct) and G5 (a model judge alone is near chance on novelty). Dedup in code; use external checks.

source: Lu et al. (2024) The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
finding: An LLM reviewer built from self-reflection, a few-shot example and ensembling reaches near-human accuracy at predicting ICLR accept/reject.
numbers: 500 ICLR 2022 papers. GPT-4o with 5 reflection rounds, 5 ensembled reviews, 1-shot: 70% accuracy; balanced accuracy 0.65 vs human 0.66; F1 0.57 vs 0.49 human; AUC 0.65 both; human accuracy 0.73 (NeurIPS 2021 consistency experiment).
quote: achieves near-human-level performance across multiple evaluation metrics (e.g. 65% vs. 66% balanced accuracy)
limits: ICLR 2022 may be in pretraining data. Accepted papers were camera-ready, rejected were original submissions (leak). Reviewer cannot see figures or ask questions. Human reviewers themselves agree poorly.
agent_relevance: A working organised-scepticism loop inside an agent: reflect, ensemble, then area-chair meta-review. The ensemble is same-model, so G4 limits apply.

source: Beel and Baumgart (2025) Evaluating Sakana's AI Scientist for Autonomous Research: Wishful Thinking or an Emerging Reality
finding: Independent evaluation of the AI Scientist found weak novelty checking, failing experiments and flawed manuscripts: a failed organised-scepticism loop.
numbers: 5 of 12 experiments (42%) failed from coding errors. Median 5 citations per paper, only 5 of 34 from 2020 or later. Ideas like micro-batching for SGD labelled novel by keyword search. Each code iteration added only 8% more characters. Some manuscripts held hallucinated numbers.
limits: Small sample (12 experiments), recommender-systems topics, one version of the system.
agent_relevance: Novelty claims checked only by keyword search pass known ideas. A sceptic step needs real retrieval plus a code-run check (G3, G2).

source: Yamada et al. (2025) The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
finding: A fully AI-generated paper was submitted to a peer-reviewed ICLR workshop and scored above the average human acceptance threshold.
numbers: One of three submitted manuscripts reached average reviewer score 6.33 (roughly top 45% of submissions) and would have been accepted after meta-review if human.
quote: first fully AI-generated paper successfully passed a rigorous peer-review process
limits: Workshop, not main conference. Three manuscripts only. Authors withdrew it before publication; organisers knew.
agent_relevance: Peer review (universalism: judged on the paper alone) can be passed by machine text; human scepticism is a weak filter at workshop level.

source: Gottweis et al. (2025) Towards an AI co-scientist
finding: Multi-agent system (generation, reflection, ranking, evolution) in a tournament: a built-in organised-scepticism loop. Search tool is what makes the novelty sceptic work.
numbers: Top-1 accuracy 78.4% on GPQA diamond picking the highest-Elo answer. Reflection agent without search rated known non-novel ideas 6.14/10 for novelty; with search 2.38/10. Correctness 7.4 to 8.46 with search. GPQA AUC 0.643 to 0.651. Debate prompt in Ranking reduced position bias.
limits: Auto-evaluation Elo is self-referential (model ranks own output); concordance with accuracy shown only on a benchmark with known answers. Ablation run with Gemini 2.0 Flash.
agent_relevance: Strongest evidence that an external search tool makes a sceptic work (2.38 vs 6.14). Matches G3: check against something the answer was not fitted to.

source: Latona et al. (2024) The AI Review Lottery: Widespread AI-Assisted Peer Reviews Boost Paper Scores and Acceptance Rates
finding: LLM-assisted reviews at ICLR 2024 were common and scored papers higher, changing acceptance near the threshold.
numbers: At least 15.8% of reviews AI-assisted (GPTZero). In 53.4% of review pairs on the same paper the AI-assisted review scored higher (p=0.002; +14.4% relative). Matched study: +4.9 percentage points acceptance (p=0.024) for papers near the threshold.
limits: Detector-based lower bound; quasi-experimental, not randomised.
agent_relevance: LLM judges are lenient. Calibrate any model grader against held-out human or code truth (G5).

source: Liang et al. (2024) Monitoring AI-Modified Content at Scale: ChatGPT impact on AI conference peer reviews
finding: Corpus-level estimate: a measurable share of peer-review text was substantially LLM-modified, higher when reviewers were low-effort.
numbers: 6.5% to 16.9% of review sentences. ICLR 2024 10.6%, NeurIPS 2023 9.1%, CoRL 2023 6.5%, EMNLP 2023 16.9%. Higher in reviews with lower confidence, submitted near deadline, from reviewers less likely to answer rebuttals.
limits: Maximum-likelihood distribution estimate, not individual detection. Before ChatGPT the estimates were about 1.6% to 2.4%.
agent_relevance: The scepticism norm erodes under effort pressure; an agent that offloads judgement to itself shows the same low-effort pattern.

source: Liang et al. (2023) Can large language models provide useful feedback on research papers? A large-scale empirical analysis
finding: GPT-4 comments overlap with human reviewers about as much as two human reviewers overlap with each other.
numbers: Nature family 3,096 papers: GPT-4 vs human 30.85%, human vs human 28.58%. ICLR 1,709 papers: 39.23% vs 35.25%; 43.80% for rejected papers. User study 308 researchers from 110 institutions: 57.4% found it helpful, 82.4% found it more beneficial than at least some human reviews.
limits: Matching pipeline F1 96.8% for extraction and 82.4% for matching. GPT-4 asks for more experiments and gives shallow critique of method design. Overlap is not correctness.
agent_relevance: A critic step finds common points but misses deep method flaws; use as a cheap first sceptic and pair with a code check.

source: Ye et al. (2024) Are We There Yet? Revealing the Risks of Utilizing Large Language Models in Scholarly Peer Review
finding: LLM reviewers favour prestigious authors and affiliations in a single-blind setting, a direct universalism violation.
numbers: 500 papers. Positive-rating ratio (score 6 or higher) rose from 36.8% to 40.8% (famous universities), 41.6% (companies), 41.2% (named authors Hinton, Bengio, LeCun).
limits: Shifts are about 4 to 5 points on 500 papers; one LLM review system tested. Author names swapped on selected papers.
agent_relevance: Measured size of authority bias in a model judge: about 4 to 5 percentage points. Supports blinding the judge (G5).

source: Ye et al. (2024) Are We There Yet? manipulation and hallucination experiments
finding: Authors can steer LLM reviews with hidden text; LLM reviewers give decent scores to incomplete or empty papers.
numbers: Manipulating 5% of reviews could make 12% of papers lose a top-30% rank. Title-only papers got a rating higher or comparable to 42% of full papers. Introduction-only content reaches over 95% of full-paper rating.
limits: Ranking effect is a simulation; prompt injection is a security issue as well as a bias issue.
agent_relevance: A model sceptic can be gamed by the artefact it reads. Graders must not trust text inside the answer (G2, G5).

source: Thakkar et al. (2025) Can LLM feedback enhance review quality? A randomized study of 20K reviews at ICLR 2025
finding: Randomised trial of an LLM Review Feedback Agent with automated reliability guardrails: reviewers updated reviews and wrote more detail.
numbers: More than 20,000 reviews randomised. 27% of reviewers who got feedback updated; over 12,000 suggestions incorporated; updated reviews +80 words vs +2 for non-updaters. Score edits 8.1% vs 7.5% (p<0.05). Over 96% of generated feedback passed all reliability tests.
limits: Feedback optional; length gain deflated by non-updaters and by 7.9% of selected reviews that got no feedback. Quality judged by blinded researchers and an LLM pipeline with 92% accuracy.
agent_relevance: Rare causal evidence that an LLM sceptic with guardrails improves human judgement. Pattern: generate, test feedback automatically, release only if all tests pass.

source: Panickssery, Bowman, Feng (2024) LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
finding: LLM judges prefer their own text (self-preference), linearly tied to how well they recognise their own output (self-recognition).
numbers: GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama 2 show self-preference on summarisation. Out of the box over 50% accuracy at telling own text from others; over 90% after fine-tuning on 500 examples (GPT-3.5, Llama 2). Self-preference strength linear in self-recognition.
limits: Two summarisation datasets (CNN/DailyMail, XSum). Causality shown by fine-tuning, not for all tasks.
agent_relevance: A violation of universalism and disinterestedness by a model judge. Backs G5: no authorship visible to a judge, and the judge should not be the author.

source: Starace et al. (2025) PaperBench: Evaluating AI's Ability to Replicate AI Research
finding: Agents replicating 20 ICML 2024 papers from scratch score far below human experts: a replication test of the sceptic norm.
numbers: 8,316 gradable tasks. Claude 3.5 Sonnet (New) 21.0%, o1 13.2%, others under 10%. Human ML PhD baseline on 3 papers (best of 3, 48 hours) 41.4%.
limits: Rubrics co-written with paper authors; LLM judge imperfect; agents often stopped early claiming completion.
agent_relevance: Agents stop early and claim done without strategy. Shows why a code-run verification step (G2, G3) is needed instead of self-report.

source: Du et al. (2024) LLMs Assist NLP Researchers: Critique Paper (Meta-)Reviewing (ReviewCritique)
finding: Expert sentence-level annotation shows LLM reviews contain more deficient segments than human reviews and are paper-unspecific and low in diversity.
numbers: Inaccurate-summary segments: 0.19% of LLM segments vs 0.36% of human segments (summary is the LLM strength). Overall LLMs produce more Deficient segments than humans; new ITF-IDF metric shows low diversity.
limits: NLP papers only, specific models; per-model deficiency rates not extracted.
agent_relevance: An LLM critic is generic. To act as a sceptic it must be forced to cite specifics from the artefact (G2).

source: Tyser et al. (2024) AI-Driven Review Systems: Evaluating LLMs in Scalable and Bias-Aware Academic Reviews
finding: Automatic review system evaluated by an arena of human preferences, planted errors, meta-prompting, role-play and venue-specific materials; discusses position and verbosity bias in LLM judges.
numbers: Cites 15.8% AI-assisted ICLR 2024 reviews. Fine-tuned predictor of which review humans prefer in head-to-head comparison. No single headline result number extracted.
limits: Abstract and setup read; results tables not extracted.
agent_relevance: Planted-error tests are a cheap measurement of a sceptic step (is the injected flaw found?). Candidate check for our scaffold.

source: Ye et al. (2024) Are We There Yet? implicit manipulation
finding: LLM reviewers reiterate limitations disclosed by authors more than human reviewers do, so authors can steer them by listing minor limitations.
numbers: Figure 11: all tested LLMs more likely than humans to repeat author-disclosed limitations; intro-only input gets over 95% of full-paper rating.
limits: Per-model percentages not extracted.
agent_relevance: If a prompt contains the proposer's own caveats, a judge tends to echo them; remove proposer commentary before judging (G5).

source: Beel and Baumgart (2025) Evaluating Sakana's AI Scientist, novelty-check design
finding: The AI Scientist labels ideas novel by up to 10 keyword search rounds; the 1-10 scores for interestingness, feasibility, novelty look arbitrary and are not used.
numbers: Up to 10 search iterations; if no clear match the idea gets novel=True. One energy-efficiency experiment reported better accuracy with more compute, against its own goal.
limits: One system version, authors' own runs.
agent_relevance: Default-to-novel when search finds nothing is a bias to avoid: absence of a match is not evidence.

source: Lu et al. (2024) The AI Scientist, calibration table and limits
finding: Authors flag leakage and design limits of the LLM reviewer; human NeurIPS baseline has high false negative rate.
numbers: Human NeurIPS baseline balanced accuracy 0.66, accuracy 0.73, F1 0.49, AUC 0.65, FPR 0.17, FNR 0.52. Random and always-reject baselines balanced accuracy 0.50.
limits: Rejected papers use original submissions, accepted use final copies, which can leak signal.
agent_relevance: Any held-out test for a sceptic needs same-format artefacts for both classes (G3).

source: Gottweis et al. (2025) Towards an AI co-scientist, tournament design
finding: Hypotheses are ranked by Elo in pairwise scientific debates; experts preferred Co-Scientist over baselines on novelty and impact.
numbers: Debate prompt beats simple comparison prompt in ranking accuracy and lowers position bias; Elo bucket tracked GPQA accuracy against a 32-sample reference per question.
limits: Expert preference study small; judge LLMs and generator share a base model family.
agent_relevance: Debate-style pairwise comparison is a design for organised scepticism; code should do the pairing and bookkeeping (G5).

source: Thakkar et al. (2025) Review Feedback Agent, reliability tests
finding: Feedback was sent only if it passed a suite of LLM-run reliability tests, so guardrails filter before a human sees it.
numbers: Over 96% passed all tests; incorporation-labelling pipeline 92% accurate; reviewers who updated raised all scores except confidence.
limits: Tests are LLM-based, not code-based.
agent_relevance: Architecture precedent for a gated critic: critique, automatic checks, then release.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) ideation agent ranker
finding: The ideation agent over-generates, dedups with embeddings, and ranks with a pairwise LLM ranker checked on ICLR submissions; prompt tricks did not help.
numbers: Claude-3.5-Sonnet zero-shot pairwise ranker 71.4% on accepted-vs-rejected ICLR pairs; GPT-4o 61.1%; Claude-3-Opus 63.5%; no significant gain from few-shot or chain-of-thought.
limits: Accuracy on ICLR pairs did not carry over to the study idea pool (53.3%).
agent_relevance: Prompt tricks did not help a judge and accuracy fell out of distribution. Justifies G3 held-out checks.

source: Liang et al. (2024) Monitoring AI-Modified Content, growth by venue
finding: Estimated LLM-modified share jumped after ChatGPT release at every venue.
numbers: ICLR 1.6% to 10.6%, NeurIPS 1.9% to 9.1%, CoRL 2.4% to 6.5%, EMNLP 2023 at 16.9%.
limits: Correlational estimate.
agent_relevance: Low-effort outputs cluster with low confidence; a confidence-based trigger for deeper checking has support (G1).
